text: A small company in a shared, indifferent sky.

Everything under this sky is shared. The air, the ducts, the hulls that creak like something asleep, and every credit anyone earns, which goes into the Common Ledger and comes back in portions. The Plan is generous. The Plan is also five cycles long, and then another five.

There is one form for leaving: a Release. It takes you off the ledger and sells you a planet nobody has counted. It is sold in credits, to fellow hands who have them.

So you have a small company, one ship's worth of cash, three planets and two goods. Buy where it is cheap. Sell where it is not. Serving the common good is encouraged. Profit, officially, is a typing error.

The sky will not notice either way.

text: More than half of Military now runs through you, and the Bureau has entered the company as supplier of record. The fleets you supply do not fire. They arrive, they are seen, and the quarrel at the border post ends by itself. The terms are posted and the ledgers can be read, which is dull, and works. Nobody in the Commons sleeps better, because nobody knows how close it was. Harrow Combine still runs its foundries, smaller and watching. The garrisons write you short letters that begin with thanks and end with a requisition.
place: End screen body, win Military, good outcome
End screen heading, win Luxury, good outcome

text: More than half of Luxury moves through you, and the doors are wide. Silk and cut glimmers went where the Plan had never thought to send beauty: the dock mess, the night shift, the school on the ring. Masks that once cost a season's rations were lent at festivals and came back with a stain and a story. Velvet Concord still keeps the grand tables, though fewer people stand at them. The Bureau drafted a form for the allocation of beauty and then, to its credit, left it blank.
place: End screen body, win Luxury, good outcome
End screen heading, win Minerals, good outcome

text: More than half of Minerals comes through you, and most of it went into ground. Ingot from the smelter, alloy from the deep cuts, plate from the fabric: the next ring of homes stands on them, with floors that do not ring when walked. The crews rotate on a posted schedule. Harrow Combine still cuts, at its own pace, in its own corner. The Bureau counted the new homes and found, to its surprise, that a form existed for them. Under the floors the stone is patient. It always was.
place: End screen body, win Minerals, good outcome
End screen heading, win Biotech, good outcome

text: More than half of Biotech passes through you, and it goes out the door. Bio-gel and gene seed reached the terraces at Tillam, the fields at Ashgate and clinics nobody had thought to supply. A cure went out on plain paper, with no licence number, and was copied by hand in rooms the Bureau never saw. Velvet Concord still sells the fine strains to those who can pay. The Plan took the credit, which is its way. In the culture lab the vats hum at the pace of something with all the time it needs.
place: End screen body, win Biotech, good outcome
End screen heading, no ship left and cash still negative (loss)

text: The company has no ships left, and the cash is still below zero. Each cycle the Bureau took the newest hull to cover the debt, and now the last is gone. Your ships are entered in the Common Ledger, and your name is given a quota that is equal and exactly the size of everyone else's. A clerk reads the closing form aloud and adds that nothing here was ever owed to you. The three rivals go on selling. The sky did not notice.
place: End screen body, no ship left and cash still negative (loss)
End screen heading, player under a tenth of every market (loss)

text: For three cycles running, your company held less than a tenth of every market, and the Bureau has stopped listing you as a competitor. The strongest of the three rivals fills the shelves where yours stood. Your ships still run, and your orders are still taken, politely, at counters that are no longer yours. Nothing cruel was done. A market is a room, and you were not in it.

End screen heading, window closed with no market held (soft ending)

text: The window closed with no market held. You did not lose. The company is solvent, the ships run, and the Bureau lists you as a participant, a word with no weight. A spread of small shares does not add up to a market. A single market, held all the way, does. The sky has no opinion. It never needed one.
place: End screen body, window closed with no market over half (soft ending)

place: End screen, above the buttons, every ending

text: The wreck of a hundred ships has settled into orbit over {planet}, hull plates and spent tanks turning slowly. A contractor will sweep it for a fee. The Bureau filed it as unowned, which is why it is still up there. The old fleets left their shortcuts behind.
Pay the fee. The debris is cleared and routes from {planet} run as before.
Routes from {planet} carry less while the debris stays. It does not clear itself.

The contractor swept the orbit and filed the receipt. Routes from {planet} carry their full load again. The wreck went somewhere. The receipt does not say where. The debt is real only while the paper is, and you stopped asking.

You left the wreck. Ships from {planet} thread around it and carry less. The offer stays open. The wreck turns slowly, a stone that has kept its place longer than any city. Neither it nor you is in a hurry.

Engineers want to put a shield across part of the sun. The residents hate it and say so in writing, at length. It would reshape the markets on planets you can buy later: some goods get cheaper, while profit and energy rise. What you already own stays as it is.
Planets you can buy later change: some resources drop, profit and energy rise.
Nothing changes. The sun keeps its full light.

The shield is up and the sky is dimmer. Residents are furious and have filed it in triplicate, in the dark. On planets you can buy later, some goods get cheaper while profit and energy climb. Planets you own are untouched. The engineers call the slow ones to keep up.
The plans go back in a drawer. The residents are relieved and file no thanks. Nothing changes in any market. An engineer asks what the rush was, and no one has an answer.

Nomad families live on the asteroids you could mine. They are not on the Common Ledger, which the Bureau takes as a personal failing. They count their people by who shares the meal. Evict them and the rock is yours. Or let them stay, and let their lamps burn.
The asteroids open for mining. Some nomads turn to piracy, and pirates rise.
The asteroids stay closed to mining. No pirates come of it.
The nomads left on the next tide, without a word. The rock is yours to mine. Some did not go far, and now they keep ships and a grudge. Pirates rise. The empty tables were left set.
You let the nomads stay. Their lamps burn on the rock, small and steady, and they share a meal with the first ship that docks. The asteroids remain closed to mining.

Pirates now work the lanes, and fewer cargoes get through. Trade volume falls while they stay. The Bureau has opened a file on them. It is a thin file, and so is the fleet behind it. Obedience is cheaper than love, and lasts as long.
Pay to have the pirates cleared. It costs credits and removes their effect on trade.

A rock is coming in on a slow path, and the Bureau noticed it the way it notices everything: late. The state can turn it aside for a fee. The form for refusing is shorter. The dark outside looks closer. The rule says wait. The rock says otherwise.
Cost: payment to the state. Asteroid dealt with. The company gains one expansion point.
An even chance: company storage is hit, or nothing happens.

The state turned the rock aside and sent a receipt. The company gains one expansion point for the trouble. The asteroid drifts on, toward someone else's sky. A law is only as strong as the person who says: this is the law.
Event reward: the asteroid is dealt with and the company gains an expansion point.

The asteroid struck {planet}. Your company storage there is gone, and what it held with it. The Bureau has recorded the loss as an adjustment of the Common Ledger. Nobody said sorry. Death takes what a life would still have held.

The asteroid grazed {planet}. Your company storage there is cracked and holds less than before. The Bureau has recorded the damage as "partial". The crack runs through the wall in a straight, patient line.

The asteroid passed the system and kept going. Nothing was hit and nothing changes. The Bureau withdrew its warning, with regret, and kept the form. You could have been struck right now. Let that decide how you read the next notice.

The first crew to cut Dross Salt on Cinderrest came up coughing. The dust is fine, white and everywhere, and the medic cannot name it. The Bureau lists Cinderrest as uninhabited, so nobody there can be ill. The crew asks whether to go on.
Dross costs more and pays more at Cinderrest for a while. Danger there rises.
Cinderrest closes for a while. Routes touching it are blocked. Danger does not rise.

The crew went back down with wet cloth over their faces. Dross at Cinderrest costs more and pays more, since fewer will cut it. The white dust settles on the lamps in even rings. The danger on Cinderrest has risen.

You called the crew up. The Bureau filed the withdrawal as a rest. Cinderrest is closed for a while, and routes touching it are blocked. The danger does not grow. Below, the dust keeps settling, as if it could wait.

A cut wall on Greywake shifted and the glass sang like a struck bell. Nothing has fallen yet, but the crack is long. Braces cost credits. The Bureau calls it a feature of the geology. The crew wants an answer before the next shift.
Costs credits now. Nullglass costs more and pays more at Greywake while the cut is slow.
Nullglass costs less and pays less at Greywake. Some of the load may be lost.

The crew set braces in rows and the wall went quiet. The work cost credits. Nullglass at Greywake costs more and pays more while the cut is slow. The glass hummed once, a low note, and then kept still.

You told them to cut. The wall held through the shift and nullglass flowed. It costs less and pays less at Greywake with so much on the dock. Some of the load may not survive the climb. The crack grew a little.
A rival eyes the dead worlds

A rival hauler pulls alongside with a message: Cinderrest and Greywake are not safe to cut alone. It offers a shared lane, the take split. Or you can outrun it and cut harder. Its hull has no name painted on it. The dust lies in the lane.
